provenance.title: The Hacking Gadgets You Need to Know

neural_graph.description: A weighted concept graph for source-grounded advisory reasoning. Weights encode relevance/confidence, not biological neurons or a trained copy of a person.

nodes.label: Classify tools by access mode
nodes.evidence: The source groups tools into hot-plug, implant, and near-access Wi-Fi categories.

nodes.label: Match the smallest suitable interface to the assessment objective
nodes.evidence: The interview presents different hardware interfaces as purpose-specific assessment platforms rather than interchangeable gadgets.

nodes.label: Learn systems through constrained interfaces
nodes.evidence: The USB Rubber Ducky discussion emphasizes learning operating-system control and keyboard-driven workflows through keystroke injection.

nodes.label: Understand protocol and OS fundamentals before relying on automation
nodes.evidence: The source repeatedly connects hardware payloads to underlying OS, embedded Linux, networking, and Wi-Fi behavior.

nodes.label: Prefer immediate field feedback when choosing portable assessment tooling
nodes.evidence: The Shark Jack Display discussion highlights on-device payload selection and result viewing without a laptop.

nodes.label: Use open community payloads as an iterative learning corpus
nodes.evidence: The closing discussion highlights the open ecosystem, community payloads, embedded Linux learning, and educational use.

nodes.label: Emulate realistic attack paths to expose defensive gaps
nodes.evidence: The interview frames the devices as penetration-testing/red-team platforms used to understand how organizations could be compromised and what should be fixed.

nodes.label: Only apply active assessment patterns to explicitly authorized systems
nodes.evidence: Source context is ethical hacking / penetration testing; GPT-DOUG-LLM keeps network execution approval-gated.

tool_class_ontology.label: Hot-plug assessment tool
tool_class_ontology.defensive_question: What trust boundary is crossed when an apparently ordinary peripheral or network accessory is connected?

tool_class_ontology.label: Pen-test implant
tool_class_ontology.defensive_question: What monitoring, physical-security, and device-control signals would reveal an unexpected inline or attached device?

tool_class_ontology.label: Near-access Wi-Fi assessment platform
tool_class_ontology.defensive_question: How resilient are managed endpoints and users when exposed to untrusted or impersonated wireless environments?

advisory_sequence: classify the requested assessment by access mode
identify the underlying OS/network/Wi-Fi trust boundary
select the least invasive observation method that can answer the question
state the defensive hypothesis before any active test
require explicit authorization before network-capable execution
collect evidence and map findings to ATT&CK/CVE/CWE/NIST objects when justified
recommend remediation and verify the fix
